articles.title: Silver lining! Preethi Pal wins second silver at Asian Para Games with sprint double
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's Preethi Pal continued her impressive run at the Asian Para Games 2026, clinching her second silver medal of the continental event with
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's Preethi Pal continued her impressive run at the Asian Para Games 2026, clinching her second silver medal of the continental event with a runner-up finish in the women's 100m T35 race on Wednesday.Preethi clocked 13.98 seconds to secure silver, adding to the medal she won in the women's 200m T35 event on Tuesday. The double podium finish further underlined the Indian para-athlete's consistency on the track.From rural Uttar Pradesh to the international podiumPreethi has overcome significant physical challenges to establish herself among India's leading para-athletes. Born into a farmer's family in rural Uttar Pradesh, she faced difficulties from birth because of weakness in her legs and an irregular leg posture.Her legs were plastered for six days after she was born, and she underwent traditional treatments in an effort to strengthen them. At the age of five, she began wearing callipers, which she continued to use for eight years.Her introduction to para-sports came at the age of 17, when videos of the Paralympic Games on social media sparked her interest in athletics. Her journey gained momentum after she met Paralympian and mentor Fathima Khatoon, who encouraged her to compete at district, state and national levels.Preethi made her international debut at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games in 2023 before making a major breakthrough at the 2024 World Para Athletics Championships, where she won bronze medals in both the 100m and 200m events.Paralympic medals and growing recordPreethi further enhanced her reputation at the Paris Paralympics in 2024, winning bronze medals in the women's 100m and 200m T35 events. She became the first Indian woman to win two track-and-field medals at a single Paralympic Games.Her achievements also include a silver and three bronze medals at the World Para Athletics Championships, four gold medals at Indian Open tournaments and a gold at the New Delhi Grand Prix.With two silver medals already secured at the Asian Para Games, Preethi has added another significant chapter to her career, demonstrating the resilience and consistency that have marked her rise in international para-athletics.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Euskadi ya es campeón del mundo: gana el oro en la cesta punta del Mundial
articles.standfirst: Xabier Barandika y Unai Lekerikabeaskoa se imponen a los hermanos Sorozabal, de Estados Unidos, en la final
articles.summary: Xabier Barandika y Unai Lekerikabeaskoase se imponen a los hermanos Sorozabal, de Estados Unidos, en la final
articles.body: Euskadi ya es campeón del mundo. La cesta punta masculina le otorga su primer título desde que la Federación Internacional de Pelota admitió como miembro de pleno derecho a la Vasca. El Mundial de Buenos Aires le ofreció sus dos primeras oportunidades de subir a lo más alto del podio en el frontón de 54 metros. En la final femenina se escenificó el primer duelo con un oro en juego entre España y Euskadi. La dupla española, formada por Erika Mugartegui y Arai Lejardi, se impuso a las vascas Maite Ortiz de Mendívil y Maia Goikoetxea por 15-9 y 15-12. Llegó el turno de los chicos. Xabier Barandika y Unai Lekerikabeaskoa se medían a los hermanos Sorozabal (Johan y Gorka), naturales de Biarritz, pero que juegan por Estados Unidos. El encuentro estuvo marcado por la igualdad. El primer set cayó del lado de la pareja vasca por 15-9. En el segundo, Barandika y Lekerika continuaron al mando. Llegaron a estar 6-2 arriba. Los Sorozabal reaccionaron con un parcial de 7-0 y, una vez por delante en el marcador, ya no cedieron y se llevaron la manga por 15-10. El tercer set (se juega a 10 puntos) resultó de lo más vibrante. Se alteraron los puntos de una y otra selección hasta que se llegó al 4-4. Barandika y Lekerika encadenaron cinco puntos seguidos para ganar el partido y dar al País Vasco el primer título mundial de su historia. "Ellos estaban cómodos con la pelota viva en el primer set, pero nosotros teníamos un punto más. En el segundo, ellos se han venido arriba. Hemos sabido luchar, pelear y defender. Lekerika ha estado como un jabato atrás. Estoy muy contento porque nos lo merecíamos", comentó Barandika en la retransmisión oficial del partido. En el partido por el bronce España se quedó sin medalla. Alex Hormaetxea y Gorka Mugartegi perdieron ante los galos Ludovic Laduche y Thibault Basque por 15-8 y 15-14. Los duelos entre España y País Vasco se suceden en Buenos Aires. Este miércoles se medirán en la semifinal del frontball masculino. También en la fase de grupos de la cesta punta femenina del frontón de 36 metros. España tendrá la oportunidad de meterse en cinco finales si supera las semifinales de frontenis masculino (ante Estados Unidos) y femenino (ante Cuba), las de paleta goma masculina (ante México) y femenina (ante Chile) y la del frontball femenino (ante Venezuela). En mano individual y parejas, este martes se dieron dos partidos entre España y Euskadi en la fase de grupos que anticiparon las finales de este viernes en las que se volverán a enfrentar. Ambos duelos cayeron del lado español. En mano parejas, Beñat Azketa y Beñat Garmendia ganaron a Igoa y Cuairan por 10-7 y 10-6. En mano individual, Gaizka Carregal (Ekhi Irribarria no pudo jugar por encontrarse indispuesto) perdió por 10-3, 4-10 y 1-5 ante España, donde Jorge Fernández jugó el primer y tercer set y Fermín Arribillaga, en el segundo.

articles.title: NHL Power Rankings: Golden Knights, Oilers Lead the Way With Hurricanes and Lightning Right Behind
articles.summary: The cream, to steal a line from Randy Savage, is beginning to rise.
articles.body:
The cream, to steal a line from Randy Savage, is beginning to rise.

The top two teams in the NHL's overall standings to begin the week were the two teams, Vegas and Carolina, that battled for the Stanley Cup a few months back. And each of the top 10 teams in terms of points percentage on Monday morning was a participant in the tournament that followed the 2025-26 season.

The B/R hockey staff was heading toward midseason form, too, as it put together the latest installment of Power Rankings.

Take a look at what we came up with and drop a thought in the app comments.

Statistics through games of Monday, Oct. 19.

ANA | BOS | BUF | CAR | CBJ | CGY | CHI | COL | DAL | DET | EDM | FLA | LAK | MIN | MTL | NJD | NSH | NYI | NYR | OTT | PHI | PIT | SEA | SJS | STL | TBL | TOR | Utah Mammoth | VAN | VGK | WPG | WSH

Their start has been lousy by any measure, but captain Drew Doughty is hoping a road trip that began Tuesday in Washington will turn things around for the Kings. "Just the boys getting together, going for dinner," he said , "it's a good time for us to gel."

They'd lost six of seven, so of course the Flames would earn win No. 2 (No. 1 on home ice) against the champs. "They're putting in a lot of good work in different areas and tonight it was nice to see them get rewarded," coach Ryan Huska said .

It's home sweet home for the Canucks, who had a minus-15 goal differential in regulation on a six-game trip. "The execution of details within our game," coach Manny Malhotra said , "things that we've continuously talked about that are just non-negotiable."

Flyers Regretting Their Offseason Moves 🤦‍♂️

Break up the Flyers, who not only defeated Colorado on Monday but also got two goals from Matvei Michkov as trade rumors swirled. "Our team goes with the young guys and the steps that they take," defenseman Travis Sanheim said .

A recent skid continued for the Penguins on Monday in Utah, and seven losses in eight games (1-6-1) were enough for coach Dan Muse to circle the wagons. "We're facing some adversity right now," he said . "We have to stay together."

A two-game win streak was ended by visiting Dallas, but coach Jeff Blashill was pleased with the opportunities the Blackhawks had. "We have to find a way to have one of those end up in the net," he said , "just from a momentum standpoint."

The difference between effort and execution was the difference between winning and losing, according to coach Rick Bowness at Minnesota. "We worked very hard," he said . "But the execution—we couldn't get any real flow going to the game."

A three-game trip that began with seven goals in a win at Ottawa ended with losses in which the Blues allowed 10 goals in Minnesota and Nashville. "We just didn't have the patience necessary to play the right way," coach Jim Montgomery said .

The skidding Ducks lost at Madison Square Garden on Monday after a 15-hour travel day thanks to an airport change and plane maintenance. "It was definitely different, but nothing you can do about it, obviously," Jackson LaCombe said .

Michigan native Alex DeBrincat signed a seven-year extension worth $91 million on Oct. 13, then began paying it off four days later with a late tying goal that enabled Detroit to beat San Jose in a shootout. "I love being a Red Wing," he said .

A 3-1-0 start devolved to .500 after a loss in Toronto in the third game of what will be six on the road before the Sharks are home on October 27. "I think we're all right," coach Ryan Warsofsky said . "We know we can feel it. We're not scoring right now."

Things changed on Tuesday night with a comeback OT win in Montreal, with Macklin Celebrini tallying twice, including the game-winner.

The Maple Leafs had lost three in a row heading into Monday (0-2-1), but all it took for Gavin McKenna was a duel with the player drafted after him in 2026. McKenna scored the game-winner against San Jose. Ivar Stenberg was minus-1 on the night.

It only took 48 hours for the Devils to tumble from a seven-goal output in a defeat of the New York Rangers to scoring just twice in a loss to Washington. "I don't know if we won a puck battle the entire second period," coach Sheldon Keefe said .

The Devils rebounded on Tuesday at home, topping the Avs.

Three straight near misses (0-1-2) came to an end for the Predators in Nashville, where they buried five of 24 shots against St. Louis. "It's a big win for us," coach Andrew Brunette said . "We've got a few days to breathe a little bit."

Consecutive losses to playoff nemesis Montreal weren't good news, but Jack Quinn pulled positives from Buffalo's in-game rallies against the Canadiens. "Just a lot of compete and the belief we have in here that we can come back in games," he said .

As nicknames go, "Mr. Saturday Night" is pretty strong. And it's well-earned for forward Cole Caufield, who scored his 66th goal in 106 Saturday games in a defeat of Buffalo. "The building's electric and these moments never get old," he said .

A weekend win at Toronto was good for the Islanders, but it didn't come without a price. Forwards Calum Ritchie and Matias Maccelli both sustained lower-body injuries that'll keep them out for a while. Ritchie is d own for 4-6 weeks; Maccelli for 2-4 .

A pleasant 3-0-1 start to a five-game road trip was spoiled a bit by an 8-3 loss at Florida, but coach Lane Lambert was taking away the positives. "(Saturday) was not good, but the trip was good," he said . "Seven out of 10 points? We'll move on."

The Kraken came home and nabbed a 4-3 shootout win over the Red Wings Tuesday.

Jamie Benn is 37 and in his 18th season, but not averse to changing things in pursuit of the Cup he's never won. "When you're younger, you just enjoy playing the game," he said , "and then the older you get, the more you appreciate the game."

Look for drama in Winnipeg when Connor Hellebuyck's suspension for failing to report to training camp reportedly ends Friday, potentially clearing the way for his return after a trade request. "I don't think our whole group is saying, 'Oh, we don't want you. We don't want you,'" coach Scott Arniel said .

Forward William Eklund's first season in an Ottawa uniform will be shorter than his teammates' thanks to a left ankle injury suffered against Philadelphia earlier this month that required surgery to repair a torn tendon. He will miss 10-12 weeks .

Even on a team with offensive talent, some games are going to come down to goalie Logan Thompson. That was the case against visiting New Jersey, when he made 29 saves in a 4-2 win. In his first four 2026-27 wins, he allowed eight goals.

What a difference a year makes for the Rangers, who couldn't buy a goal or a win at Madison Square Garden early last season, but are 6-0-0 there to start 2026-27. They didn't win a sixth home game in 2025-26 until Jan. 26.

The Avalanche are one of the league's elites. But that doesn't mean they can simply show up and win, as evidenced by a road loss to Philadelphia. "Sluggish and sloppy," coach Jared Bednar said . "Execution was a big factor. Sloppy."

Just when it looked like Brady Tkachuk might have forgotten how to play productive hockey, he remembered. The first-year Panther became the third player in NHL history with back-to-back natural hat tricks against Columbus and Vancouver.

Goalie Sebastian Cossa got in for the streaking Mammoth and picked up his first home win in Utah on Monday. "Great, great win by (Cossa)," coach Andre Tourigny said . "Good to get a win in front of our fans for him. A heck of a performance."

It's hard to imagine a better sendoff for a five-game road trip than a fourth straight home win, which is what the Wild got against Columbus. Minnesota won 23 games at home (10th in the NHL) and 23 on the road (seventh in the NHL) in 2025-26.

The streak did come to an end up on Tuesday in an OT loss in Edmonton.

The Bruins made one of the league's longest trips to California but came away with three wins after beating San Jose, Anaheim, and Los Angeles. Boston was tied for 26th in the league last season with just 16 road wins in 41 games.

Nikita Kucherov will soon become the Lightning's all-time point-getter. Tyler Johnson saw it coming when 'Kuch' was a kid. "You could just see how detailed he was in everything he did," he said . "He was thinking about the smallest of things."

A seven-game win streak that included a franchise-best five on the road for the reigning champs came to an end in Calgary, of all places. "You've got to figure it out," coach Rod Brind'Amour said . "This is the no-one-feels-sorry-for-you league."

Don't feel too bad. The Canes rebounded on Tuesday with a big win against the Canucks.

Connor McDavid is playing on another level, even for him. He became the fastest player to 20 points since Mario Lemieux did so during the 1995-96 season. "Everybody is playing really well," he said , "doing things detailed, structured, playing hard."

Goals were coming easily for the Golden Knights, who netted six in consecutive defeats of Calgary and Pittsburgh and 17 across three games. "We've had good starts," forward Jack Eichel said . "We're getting pucks to the net and making plays."

articles.title: Swimming in success: Ravi Budigina claims silver in 100m backstroke, Himanshu Nandal wins bronze in 100m breaststroke at Para Asian Games
articles.summary: Indian swimmer Himanshu Nandal won his second bronze medal at the Asian Para Games after finishing third in the men's 100m breaststroke S11 event in
articles.body: Indian swimmer Himanshu Nandal won his second bronze medal at the Asian Para Games after finishing third in the men's 100m breaststroke S11 event in Nagoya on Wednesday.The 22-year-old from Rohtak, Haryana, clocked 1:20.72 seconds. Nandal has been completely visually impaired since birth due to optic nerve failure. China's Yang Bozun won gold in a Games-record time of 1:12.69, while Japan's Keiichi Kimura took silver in 1:12.72.Nandal had won his first medal on Tuesday, finishing third in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event with a timing of 5:10.91 in a four-swimmer field.Coming from a family with a sporting background, Nandal drew inspiration from his father, who played hockey at the national level. He moved to Delhi at the age of four and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille.Nandal graduated in political science from Delhi University's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College. He initially took up judo and won medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.In 2024, he became the first Indian blind swimmer to achieve the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.The S11 classification in para swimming is for athletes with severe visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Ravi Budigina wins second silverRavi Budigina claimed his second silver medal at the Asian Para Games, finishing second in the men's 100m backstroke S13 final with a time of 1:10.10.Uzbekistan's Egor Bolotov won gold in an Asian-record time of 58.43 seconds, finishing 11.67 seconds ahead of Budigina.Budigina had earlier won silver in the men's 100m freestyle S13 event on Monday.The S13 classification is for athletes with visual impairment who have the least vision loss among athletes eligible to compete in a Paralympic sport.Rohit Kumar wins Bronze in Men's 100m Breaststroke SB4 FinalRohit Kumar clinched a bronze medal in the men's 100m breaststroke SB4 final, clocking 1:57.25. The Indian was fourth at the 50m mark, narrowly trailing Saudi Arabia's Hussain Al-Rashid, but produced a strong finish to secure bronze by a margin of 1.17 seconds.Rohit was never in contention for the gold, which went to Malaysia's Muhammad Bin Zulkafli in a Games-record time of 1:41.44.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mark Allen: Snooker star thanks fans day after NI Open exit and says he can 'see the light' amid mental health struggles
articles.summary: Mark Allen has assured fans he is "doing his best" amid mental health struggles; Allen told reporters his career could be over after exiting the Northern Ireland Open on Tuesday; If you are affected by this story, please visit sky.com/viewersupport
articles.body:
Allen cast doubt on his snooker career following defeat at the Northern Ireland Open, telling TNT Sports he "doesn't see a future with snooker in it" in an emotional interview that sparked a considerable deal on online support for the world No 12.

The Antrim native was playing his first match since his World Championship semi-final loss to Wu Yize in April - when he missed a match-ball black off the spot at 16-15 in front and went on to lose a decider.

The 40-year-old has since stayed away from the tour due to personal issues that he has kept private, but are understood not to relate to any repercussions from the manner of his defeat at the Crucible.

On Wednesday, Allen released a statement via social media thanking everyone for their messages after his interview the previous day, and reassuring fans that his current mental state is the best it's been in months after receiving care.

"Everything I said in that interview was true," Allen wrote. "However, rest assured I'm doing my best to turn things around," he said.

"I have been in a mental health clinic for the last 10 weeks, finally discharging so I could attempt to play in Belfast.

"I owed that to my family, in particular my daughter to see me play for what could be the last time….. I also owed it to the fans who have supported me throughout my 21 years on tour.

"I'm not okay, but I'm okay in that itself. I've been much worse in the last few months than you saw yesterday. I literally didn't see a future in anything…

'My daughter kept me going, the therapists, staff and all the other patients were amazing and helped me through some really dark days.

"I see the light now that I couldn't see before but I do now. I also know it won't happen overnight. I'm a work in progress!!! My fight and determination on the table has always been there for ones to see. I need to show those same fighting qualities off it now for a while."

Allen has been among the world's top players for a long time, winning both UK and Masters titles in a total of 12 ranking tournament wins, and has reached the world championship semi-finals three times.

He also praised close friend and fellow Antrim native Jordan Brown, to whom he lost on Tuesday, for his conduct during their match, before thanking fans for their continued support in the face of his struggles:

"Please don't detract anything from Jordan yesterday, he's been aware of my struggles and that can't have been easy to play in but he handled it with grace and skill as I knew he would. I'm proud to call him a friend.

"I hope the rest of the event is a success and I will continue my treatments going forward and then see what's ahead.

"Thank you to every single message I have received on here [X], Instagram, Facebook, text messages and WhatsApps, I've seen them all but a bit overwhelmed to reply right now.

"Just know that they have helped me a lot but I'm not going anywhere just yet!!!! I have so much to live for and this is only the beginning of my new journey.

"Also, I was not made to do any interviews [on Tuesday], I was simply given a choice and felt I owed it to everyone to speak. The media team at WST have been incredible through all this too. Thank you all.

What did Allen say in his original interview?

In his original interview with TNT Sports directly after his defeat, Allen said he was "really overwhelmed" after his first match back on the tour in six months.

"I'm in a bad place at the minute, so even just to go out there and try was tough.

"I think if I wasn't playing Jordan I wouldn't have come back. I felt like if I was going to play one last time, playing here at the Waterfront, where it all started in 2005, against one of my best mates, I thought that was a better way to sign out."

Asked if he was serious about his threat to retire, Allen confirmed his view and continued: "I've been flooded with support but the problems are within. I just don't see a future with snooker in it, if I'm honest.

"It's sad to say, because it's all I've loved to do since I was 12 but the last few months has been really difficult and it's put snooker into perspective for me. At the minute I'm just trying to survive."

Both World Snooker Tour and the sport's governing body, the WPBSA, have provided support to Allen and have indicated their desire to continue helping him in any way they can.

articles.title: La DGT multa a 29 conductores que fumaban al volante: ¿es ahora ilegal conducir fumando?
articles.standfirst: La última campaña de vigilancia de las distracciones se ha saldado con 9.245 denuncias, y el hecho de que se hayan puesto 29 multas "por fumar" plantea una duda: ¿pueden multarte por encender un cigarrillo mientras conduces?
articles.summary: La última campaña de vigilancia de las distracciones se ha saldado con 9.245 denuncias, y el hecho de que se hayan puesto 29 multas "por fumar" plantea una duda: ¿pueden multarte por encender un cigarrillo mientras conduces?
articles.body: La DGT ha publicado los resultados de su última campaña de vigilancia y control de las distracciones al volante, que ha llevado a cabo entre los días 5 y 11 de octubre. Durante esa semana, los agentes de la Agrupación de Tráfico de la Guardia Civil controlaron 422.927 vehículos y formularon 9.245 denuncias por conductas que pueden comprometer la atención por parte del conductor. El mal uso del teléfono móvil volvió a ser el principal motivo de sanción, con 3.816 denuncias que representan el 41,3% del total de las 9.245 denuncias interpuestas. Tras el móvil, las conductas más sancionadas fueron conducir con cascos o auriculares, con 441 denuncias, y abrocharse el cinturón de seguridad una vez iniciada la conducción, con 421. Sin embargo, entre los datos de la campaña hay uno que llama especialmente la atención. La DGT recoge 29 denuncias "por fumar" al volante. ¿Significa esto que está prohibido conducir mientras se fuma y que basta con llevar en la mano un cigarrillo encendido para recibir una multa, como sucede con el teléfono móvil? Eso es lo que vamos a aclarar. La respuesta es no. En España, fumar mientras se conduce no constituye por sí mismo una infracción de tráfico. No existe una prohibición específica que impida encender un cigarrillo al volante. Lo que sí establece el Reglamento General de Circulación, en su artículo 18.1, es que el conductor debe mantener su libertad de movimientos, el campo de visión necesario y la atención permanente a la conducción para garantizar su propia seguridad y la del resto de los usuarios de la vía. Es decir, que el hecho de fumar no debe entorpecer la conducción. Un agente no denuncia a un conductor por el simple hecho de verlo fumar, sino porque entiende que su manera de hacerlo compromete su seguridad o la del resto de conductores o peatones. Es lo que puede suceder al buscar el paquete de tabaco, manipular un mechero, encender el cigarrillo o sacudir la ceniza mientras se circula. O cuando el conductor pierde el control del coche al intentar sacudirse una brasa que ha caído sobre su ropa o el asiento. Pero tampoco se puede afirmar que cualquiera de estas acciones implique automáticamente una sanción. Lo determinante es cómo afecta a la conducta del conductor y qué hechos concretos observa el agente. Sujetar un cigarrillo con una mano, por ejemplo, no constituye por sí solo una infracción si no se comprometen las condiciones de seguridad que exige la normativa de tráfico. Por eso, la formulación de la DGT al incluir 29 denuncias "por fumar" en su balance puede pecar de demasiado simplificada. Es evidente que un comunicado no puede detallar qué hizo cada uno de esos conductores. Pero cabe entender que el agente debió entender en estas ocasiones que el conductor estaba distraído, aunque las circunstancias de cada denuncia son las que determinarían si existía una infracción sancionable. Cuando la actuación al fumar se considera conducción negligente, la multa puede ascender a 200 euros, sin pérdida de puntos. En cualquier caso, el importe depende de la infracción concreta que se denuncie, porque no es lo mismo apartar más de lo necesario la vista para encender un cigarrillo, que estar a punto de causar un accidente al salirse del carril o saltarse un semáforo en rojo por no haberlo visto. Hay, además, una diferencia enorme entre fumar y arrojar la colilla por la ventanilla. La ley sí contempla expresamente la conducta de arrojar a la vía o sus inmediaciones objetos que puedan provocar incendios o accidentes. En ese caso, la infracción es muy grave y conlleva una multa de 500 euros y la retirada de seis puntos del carné.

articles.title: Don't Be Fooled, The Bloodline Will Destroy The 946 at WWE Survivor Series
articles.summary: The arrival of The 946 on WWE has brought superb television, thanks to the group's unique presentation, fresh production tactics, and a creative team that has brought out the best in The Bloodline up to this point in their rivalry.
articles.body:
The arrival of The 946 on WWE has brought superb television, thanks to the group's unique presentation, fresh production tactics, and a creative team that has brought out the best in The Bloodline up to this point in their rivalry.

Though nothing has been announced officially, all signs point to a showdown in War Games between the two factions. While Royce Keys, Lucien Prince, Bronco Nima, Carmelo Hayes and Jaida Parker have brought an air of freshness to WWE, make no mistake about it: The Bloodline will destroy the faction at Survivor Series.

That is not an indictment of the newly formed group, either.

Debating Triple H's Obsession With WarGames Match 👨‍⚖️

Keys and Co. have been spectacular. They have grabbed the ball and run with it, oftentimes resulting in the best segment of any WWE Raw episode. They have been menacing, physical, and violent when necessary, and have presented a front against The Bloodline that fans can buy into as being legitimate.

Keys looks the part of a dominant big man who can stand across the ring from Roman Reigns and throw fists. Nima and Prince may be inexperienced, but they have held up their end of the bargain. Hayes is almost too good to be involved as just another face in a faction, but it has helped lift him out of the creative abyss he found himself in and relocated him to the main event.

Then there is Parker, whose on-screen aura is that of a star. She may be the biggest name of the bunch when all is said and done.

No, The 946 will be destroyed at Survivor Series because that is the nature of things in WWE.

The group has been heated up and introduced to the fans with the sole purpose of ultimately putting The Bloodline over in a high-profile match. No match is more significant to feuding factions than War Games.

As if there were not already a perceived hierarchy difference between the two groups, the Bloodline is led by the biggest star in the company, Reigns. The same Reigns who has dominated WWE as The Tribal Chief for the last five years. He rarely loses big matches and is in the midst of his greatest run to date, delivering consistent Match of the Year candidates in his World Heavyweight Championship defenses.

With Reigns appearing to be a collision course with Oba Femi at WrestleMania 43, management in the company is going to look to keep The OTC as strong as possible, and that is unlikely to include a War Games loss to a 946 faction that does not currently have clear direction even beyond its feud with Reigns and Co.

Add to that a storyline that sets up for at least one big return in the form of former women's world champion Naomi, who can confront and take out Parker, and you have a scenario that sets up for The Bloodline to stand tall.

The only saving grace for The 946 could be the role of Jacob Fatu.

Parker ran over The Samoan Werewolf in her main roster debut, and while that would seemingly lead to him siding with his cousins, there is history with Keys that could lead him to align with the heels.

Especially considering his role in The Bloodline was against his will and the result of a loss to Reigns.

Barring some major storyline swerve or the decision to add LA Knight to The 946 team at Survivor Series and get his win back from Money in the Bank, Reigns, The Usos and Solo Sikoa will pick up the win at Survivor Series.

The feud may continue, with televised tag matches eating up TV time to close out the year, as is usual with the holidays coming, but the feud will be largely over and The Bloodline will move on to whatever plans WWE has in store for it on the road to WrestleMania.

articles.title: Asian Para Games: Simran, Praveen Kumar, Sachin Khilari shine as India's medal tally swells to 62
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a memorable Day 3 at the Asian Para Games 2026, with its athletics contingent leading the charge with five gold medals among 18
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a memorable Day 3 at the Asian Para Games 2026, with its athletics contingent leading the charge with five gold medals among 18 podium finishes to help the country swell its overall medal tally to 62 and climb to fifth in the standings.Sprinter Simran, high-jumper Praveen Kumar and shot-putter Sachin Khilari set new Games records in their respective events, while Dilip Gavit and Ayush Verma also struck gold as Indian athletes dominated the track and field competitions in Aichi-Nagoya on Wednesday.India's overall tally stood at 14 gold, 22 silver and 26 bronze medals, with athletics accounting for 13 gold, 14 silver and 15 bronze. Beyond athletics, India also added medals in para-archery, para-swimming and powerlifting, while the badminton contingent assured itself of further podium finishes.Simran's record-breaking double, Gavit and Praveen shineSimran was among India's standout performers, winning the women's 100m T12 gold in a Games-record time of 12.02 seconds. The visually impaired sprinter had also claimed the women's 200m T12 gold with a Games record on Tuesday, completing a memorable sprint double.She finished ahead of Iran's Hajar Safarzadeh, who clocked 12.30 seconds, while Indonesia's Made Ni Putri took bronze in 12.51 seconds.Dilip Gavit won the men's 100m T47 gold in 10.69 seconds, leading a one-two finish for India. Mohammed Morssinganakath Basil took silver in 10.72 seconds, a Games record, while China's Kangjun Shi secured bronze in 10.80 seconds.Praveen Kumar won gold in the men's high jump T44/64 event with a Games-record performance, while Sachin Khilari claimed the top spot in the men's shot put F46. Ayush Verma also won gold in the men's shot put F53 event.India collected four athletics silver medals in the morning session through Banti in the men's high jump T44/64, Bhagyashri Jadhav in the women's shot put F34, Mohd Yasser in the men's shot put F46 and Manjeet in the men's javelin F12/13.The bronze medallists included Anubhav Choudhary in the men's 100m T35, Parveen in the men's shot put F46 and Rakeshbhai Bhatt in the men's 100m T37.Preethi Pal adds second silver; athletics haul reaches 42Preethi Pal continued her impressive campaign by winning silver in the women's 100m T35, adding to the silver she claimed in the 200m T35 on Tuesday. The double bronze medallist at the 2024 Paris Paralympics was among three Indian athletes to have won two medals at the Games so far.India's athletics contingent had accumulated 42 medals by Wednesday, keeping it on course for its ambitious target of winning medals in 60 of the 62 events it is contesting.Sheetal Devi, swimmers and powerlifter add to India's tallyArmless compound archer Sheetal Devi and Payal Nag won silver in the women's doubles event after losing to China in the final.In para-swimming, visually impaired Ravi Kartik Budigina secured his second silver of the Games, finishing runner-up in the men's 100m backstroke S13 in 1:10.10. Himanshu Nandal also won his second medal, taking bronze in the men's 100m breaststroke S11 in 1:20.72.Powerlifter Kasthuri Rajamani claimed silver in the women's 67kg category, marking the biggest achievement of her career.In badminton, India's men's singles SL4 campaign was guaranteed at least three medals after defending champion Suhas L Y, Naveen Sivakumar and Abhijeet Sakhuja advanced to the semifinals. The SL4 classification covers athletes with moderate lower-limb impairments.Krishna Nagar and Sivarajan Solaimalai secured silver in the men's doubles SH6 category. With four pairs competing in a single group, medals were awarded according to the final group standings rather than through knockout matches.India builds momentum with more medals in sightIndia's strong showing across disciplines has strengthened its position in the overall standings, with athletics providing the biggest boost. The five gold medals won on Wednesday took the country's gold tally to 14, while the overall count reached 62.With more competition remaining before the event concludes on Saturday, India will look to build on its momentum and add to its medal haul across athletics, badminton, swimming and other disciplines.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dominik Mysterio Talks WWE 2K26 Street Fighter DLC, Rey Mysterio, AAA, Judgment Day in B/R Interview
articles.summary: Another chapter is set to be written in WWE's working relationship with the Street Fighter video game franchise this month, and this time it involves "Dirty" Dominik Mysterio.
articles.body:
Another chapter is set to be written in WWE's working relationship with the Street Fighter video game franchise this month, and this time it involves "Dirty" Dominik Mysterio.

Mysterio is one of five WWE Superstars who will be included in the WWE 2K26 x Street Fighter Elite DLC Pack, which features wrestlers playing the roles of Street Fighter characters.

Dom is cast as Ken, and he's joined by Rey Mysterio as Ryu, Bianca Belair as Cammy, The Rock as M. Bison and Ultimate Warrior as Blanka.

The characters in the game are modeled specifically after WWE Mattel action figures depicting Superstars as Street Fighter characters, which makes it extra special from Dominik's perspective.

"I've been in a couple of 2K games with WWE the past couple years now, but this is special," Mysterio said. "It's Street Fighter, it's not only a DLC pack that you have to pre-order and get separately, but also they made it an action figure. I have a couple at the house, and it's in, like, an old arcade-style box, and they're super cool. I have a couple in my game room, and it's just cool to be a part of the whole Street Fighter franchise."

Dirty Dom revealed that he wasn't told about the Ken action figure ahead of time and didn't know about it until he saw photos. At that point, he instantly wanted to get one in his possession.

"I didn't know until I started getting tagged in the pictures of me as Ken, and I was like, 'What is going on? Did someone make this custom, or like, what is it,'" Mysterio said. "And then the company ended up telling me, like, 'Oh no, you're part of this DLC pack in 2K26.' And I was like, 'What? This is so sick.' I found out kind of like the old-fashioned way where I just kept getting tagged. And then as soon as I saw it, I was like, 'How do I get my hands on this action figure?'"

Ken has long been among the most popular characters in the Street Fighter video game franchise, which first launched in 1987 and truly rose to prominence with the release of Street Fighter II in 1991.

Dominik feels he and Ken have some similarities, noting that Ken's bio describes him as a fighter who comes to the United States to "get humbled because he's too cocky."

Dom also acknowledged that both he and Ken have luscious heads of hair, quipping that he may have to "golden up the tips of the good old mullet" at some point in order to match Ken.

Fittingly, Mysterio likes to play the Street Fighter video game series with some of his fellow WWE Superstars, and Ken is his character of choice when his back is against the wall in a "glass break in case of emergency" situation since he knows how to do all of his combos.

Dirty Dom called the chance to play as himself dressed like Ken in WWE 2K26 a "surreal" experience, although he didn't seem particularly thrilled to have to share the honor with his WWE Hall of Fame father, Rey Mysterio.

Ken and Ryu are best friends bordering on brothers in Street Fighter lore, and although Dominik and Rey are related by blood, they've been fierce, on-screen rivals for the past several years.

Often referring to Rey as his "deadbeat dad," Dominik expressed excitement over the chance to rough Rey up, whether it is in WWE 2K26 or in reality.

"Of course, I would do it in the game and real life," Dom said of beating up his dad. "Even if I gotta get a red gi and show up at his house and, you know, hit him with a good, old-fashioned swift kick. But yeah, I would definitely do some damage because he doesn't play video games. I'm an avid gamer myself, so I would put belt to ass."

Dominik went on to say that Rey has never beaten him in a video game, and that he is a "compulsive liar" if he suggests otherwise.

In addition to the excitement of being a key part of WWE's tie-in with Street Fighter, the younger Mysterio has some big things on the horizon from an in-ring perspective.

It starts with Héroes Inmortales on Saturday at Gimnasio Olímpico Juan de la Barrera in Mexico City when he challenges El Grande Americano for the AAA Mega Championship.

Grande beat Dominik for the AAA mega title at Triplemanía 34 last month, ending his yearlong reign as champion.

Americano was aided by Rey Mysterio in that match, as the AAA general manager replaced the incapacitated referee and made the three count that crowned Grande the new champion.

Dom expects things to be different this time around, though, and he called his shot by predicting that he will become a two-time AAA mega champion.

"At Triplemanía we had an unauthorized referee that came in and made the count, so it shouldn't have counted," Dominik said. "And plus, Juan de la Barrera is Dirty Dom town when it comes to Mexico City, so he'd better come prepared because I'm taking what's mine, that's the AAA Mega Campeonato."

Along with his work in AAA, Mysterio has long been a fixture on the Raw roster as part of The Judgment Day stable with Liv Morgan, Raquel Rodriguez, Roxanne Perez and JD McDonagh.

Dominik is a two-time intercontinental champion, so it comes as little surprise that he has his sights set on getting his hands on championship gold once again in the near future.

"There's a lot of things I'd like to get done," Mysterio said. "I got some beef with [world heavyweight champion] Roman [Reigns] kind of. He tried to throw me out of the ring and end my career one time. Sami Zayn, on the other hand, we've got a lot of history with Sami and Kevin [Owens] in The Judgment Day, so maybe there's something over there with the WWE title on the line. Maybe I want my IC title back. Maybe I wanna go for the tag titles with JD, get him some gold too. Who knows? There's a lot of things I'd like to get done, but we're taking it one day at a time."

Dirty Dom seemingly always finds a way to get himself in the mix, and it will undoubtedly be worth watching what kinds of moves he makes on Raw in the weeks and months to come.

Until then, Mysterio is focused on regaining the AAA Mega Championship and doing some damage as the Ken version of himself in WWE 2K26.

The WWE 2K26 x Street Fighter Elite Pack officially drops on Oct. 28, complete with five unique characters, as well as special signature moves and 15 Create-a-Superstar parts related to iconic Street Fighter characters.

articles.title: Ty Dieffenbach will have 'at least' one more year of eligibility
articles.summary: New UCLA starting quarterback Ty Dieffenbach will have at least one more season of NCAA eligibility after the 2026 season.
articles.body:
How much more of Ty Dieffenbach should UCLA Bruin fans expect to see? A whole lot. Bob Chesney announced that Nico Iamaleava is undergoing surgery and will be out for UCLA , leaving the starting spot open for Dieffenbach to take advantage of.

Dieffenbach has passed his first two tests, holding off the Oregon Ducks in Autzen Stadium and then defeating the Wisconsin Badgers to move the Bruins to 6-0. Not only can Dieffenbach stick around this season for UCLA, he could potentially be with the team next season as well.

California Post reporter Ben Bolch reported that Dieffenbach will have "at least" one more season of NCAA eligibility following the 2026 season. Dieffenbach is in his fourth season of college football but just his second with game action.

Dieffenbach did not play in his two seasons with Pittsburgh before transferring and starting last season with Cal Poly. Following the season with the Mustangs, Dieffenbach joined UCLA to battle for a spot as Iamaleava's backup.

Dieffenbach was battling against Iamaleava's young brother, Madden Iamaleava, for the second-string spot but now he'll have a chance to start for the Bruins for at least the remainder of the season.

So far this season, Dieffenbach has thrown for one touchdown, one interception with 307 passing yards, going 25-39 through the air. Dieffenbach is a tall quarterback, standing at 6'6", and has shown tremendous arm talent in his six quarters of game action with UCLA.

articles.title: Five major concerns for Penn State after their bye week
articles.summary: Penn State enters the bye week with major concerns regarding quarterback play and a struggling run game.
articles.body:
There seems to be a problem with everything surrounding the Nittany Lions as they approach this bye week with more questions than answers. The team looks entirely different from the squad that started out 3-0 and as of right now, they're closer to missing a bowl altogether than to getting their season back on track. While they certainly have some winnable games on the back half of their schedule, they have given fans no reason to believe in any sort of rebound. Here are five major concerns the Nittany Lions must address during and even after this bye week.

Not even the most casual of Penn State fans can act like Becht has been anything but abysmal over these past four weeks. He looks nothing like the quarterback that started out the season with no turnovers during their nonconference slate. In fact, ever since their last nonconference game against Buffalo, Becht has thrown five interceptions. Against Michigan, you could say he was the sole reason that the Wolverines got back into the game in the second half, as all 21 of their points can be attributed to a Becht turnover. If this situation does not get figured out soon, fans will not be scared to voice their opinion.

Another issue stemming from the offense and perhaps the reason for Becht's struggles is the ineptitude of the run game. Consider the fact that in 16 straight quarters, the Nittany Lions running backs have failed to have a carry for over 10 plus yards. They have averaged an abysmal 2.2 yards per carry in their Big Ten games and 78 yards per game. It seems as if a room with a lot of different traits is struggling to find the best one to bring out an identity that works. Taylor Mouser has a lot of work to do if he really wants this running game to ever get off the ground.

This always seems to be a problem for the blue and white no matter who's coaching them these days. For some reason, whenever they get inside the twenty yard line, they never seems to put up touchdowns. While Ryan Barker is a fine kicker, Penn State fans are probably tired of seeing him trot out there more often than not after another failed drive in the red zone. The Nittany Lions have somehow 28 red zone trips into only 15 touchdown drives. Considering the fact that the offense already struggles as a whole, it doesn't make matters any better.

While the offense seemingly has more problems, that does not mean that the defense has not had many either. One of the most glaring ones stems from up front and the lack of production from what was thought to be a strength of this team. While players like Dani Dennis-Sutton and Abdul Carter are not in Happy Valley anymore, a deep rotation up front was expected to produce. That has so far not been the case. The defense has only managed 9 sacks and seven of those have come from linebackers. In fact, Caleb Bacon , who accounts for one of the two remaining sacks, was converted to be an edge rusher from the linebacker position. If the actual D-line can't do its job, it puts unnecessary pressure on the entire defensive unit.

Another problem that stems from both units' issues is Penn State's turnover margin. Sitting at minus-1, it is not indicative of a team that both takes care of the football and takes it away. Sure, there have been bright spots in the secondary, like freshman Josiah Zayas , but when the offense keeps turning the ball over themselves, whatever hard work the defense does gets erased just as quickly. Penn State needs to put itself into more situations where the offense can benefit from defensive takeaways and the defense doesn't have to feel the pressure of making up for the offense's mistakes.

articles.title: FIA introduces strict rules to prevent ‘tricks’ within the cost cap regulations
articles.summary: The FIA is significantly tightening the rules for Formula 1 teams from 2027 onwards. The motorsport federation wants to prevent teams from gaining an advanta...
articles.body:
The FIA is significantly tightening the rules for Formula 1 teams from 2027 onwards. The motorsport federation wants to prevent teams from gaining an advantage through other projects within their organisations that fall outside the cost cap. The measures go so far that they could even affect where employees are allowed to work.

The cost cap limits how much teams can spend on their Formula 1 operations. Its purpose is to prevent the wealthiest teams from investing unlimited funds in their performance. Enforcement becomes more complicated, however, when an organisation has departments working on other technologies alongside its F1 team.

Red Bull, for example, has its 'Advanced Technologies' division, Mercedes has 'Applied Science', and Aston Martin has 'Performance Technologies'. Ferrari is also working on the Hypersail sailing project. These activities are separate from Formula 1, but the technical expertise they develop could also be of interest to the racing departments.

That is the FIA's concern. An employee could officially be working on a project outside Formula 1 while their expertise also benefits the F1 team. The associated costs would then remain outside the cost cap, even as the team benefits from their work. However, there is no proof that teams have actually broken the rules in this way.

The FIA has previously introduced measures to prevent such arrangements. For example, technical expertise transferred to the F1 team from another department had to be counted towards the cost cap. It was also stipulated that the full salaries of employees contributing to F1 activities must fall within the spending limit. From 2027, the governing body is going a step further. A new 12-page chapter in the operational regulations requires a strict separation between the F1 department and employees working on other projects.

The FIA has significantly tightened a number of rules - Photo: Red Bull Content Pool

This means, among other things, that the two groups will no longer be allowed to work in the same office. Factories must be divided into restricted-access zones with electronic entry controls. Teams must retain access logs for three years so the FIA can later check who entered which areas. Facilities such as wind tunnels, simulators and engine test benches may still be used by both departments under certain conditions. However, employees from the two groups may not be present at the same time, and no information may be exchanged.

Restrictions will also apply to shared spaces. Employees can still have lunch together in the canteen, but they may not carry out their actual work there. The same applies to other shared areas, such as corridors and car parks.

Separate offices alone are not enough. IT systems must also be kept apart so employees cannot access information belonging to the other department. Teams may not circumvent the restrictions through messaging services, external storage devices or contractual arrangements either. Under limited circumstances, expertise may be transferred from the F1 department to a project outside Formula 1.

The reverse route is also being closed off: information from those other projects may not flow to the F1 team. The FIA wants to prevent an organisation from conducting research outside the cost cap and then using the results to make its Formula 1 car faster.

Formula 1 teams face further restrictions related to the budget cap - Photo: Red Bull Contentpool

Moving between departments within the same company will become harder

The transfer of employees between departments will also be restricted. Anyone moving to the F1 team from a project outside of the competition must first complete a three-month period without any work, and during that time, the employee is barred from accessing the restricted IT systems. They must then commit contractually to working exclusively on F1-related matters for at least 12 months.

Strict conditions will apply to moves in the opposite direction as well. An F1 employee moving to another technical department must receive a new contract, revised access rights and a new email address. That employee must then work exclusively for the new department for 12 months. Their salary will also continue to count towards the F1 cost cap for that year. This means a team cannot simply move staff to another department during the season to free up cap space.

articles.title: Adriana Díaz: Ohio State women’s basketball 2026-27 player preview
articles.summary: If what Adriana Díaz’s teammates say is true, the Spanish international will begin a historic career as a Buckeye freshman
articles.body:
The game of college basketball requires more in 2026 than it did 20 years ago.

In the past, head coaches brought in groups of freshmen to build out a mini dynasty over four years. Some years would be lighter than others to ensure playing time, development and maintaining a winning culture.

Today, with the ability to transfer there are multiple ways to build out a team each year. Some programs build out new teams basically each season.

For Ohio State women's basketball, who returned eight of their 11 players from last season, and four of five starters, this would be considered a light recruiting year. The transfer portal did not yield any results for head coach Kevin McGuff and the program landed three freshmen in a program that does not usually rely heavily on younger players.

Of those three freshmen, one has already stood out to not only those that recruited her but everyone who steps onto the court alongside her. Adriana Díaz is a Spanish international who enters Ohio State ready to make an impact on day one.

Name: Adriana Díaz Position: Forward Class: Freshman High School: Movistar Estudiantes Madrid (Madrid, Spain) 2025-26 Stats: 12.0 ppg, 7.0 rpg, 1.0 apg

In April, Díaz committed to Ohio State. In August, Díaz was with the Spanish youth national team at the U18 Eurobasket Championship for her second year in a row.

Much like 2025, Spain rolled through competition to win its seventh gold medal at the U18 level. Part of that was the play of Díaz.

The big averaged 19.9 minutes per game. In that time, Díaz averaged 8.9 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game. In the quarter-finals against Italy, Díaz had 10 points, 6 rebounds, 3 steals and 2 assists and an astounding +43 +/-, which means that when she was on the court, Spain outscored Italy by 43 points.

Watch an Ohio State women's basketball game and the predominant strategy is to play strong defense, force turnovers and turn those turnovers into easy points. That's in the full court.

Once the Buckeyes get to the half court, movement and leaving space under the basket helps let players like point guard Jaloni Cambridge find space and make plays. That includes sometimes parking outside of the arc, running to the basket and dishing out for three-point opportunities.

Díaz can do all of that. The steals. The speed in transition. The running to the basket. The passing. The shooting from beyond the arc. All of it.

"You gonna have to play this video back in four years, but no one's seen it yet. But AD [Díaz], she's going to be one of the best Buckeyes to ever come out of here," Kennedy Cambridge told reporters. "She came in first day, I literally looked at her and was like, 'Yeah, we're gonna be great.' Man, like, but also, with her being bigger, she can guard, she can shoot. She's so strong too, y'all. I really don't even understand."

"I took a charge on her, and I'll never do that again," Jaloni Cambridge added.

When people reference a European big, they think of somebody who has an all-around game. Someone who can use their strength inside and also hit midrange baskets or deep shots. Díaz fits that definition and she can also go to the basket without the sometimes awkwardness that comes with size for a college basketball player.

At 6-foot-1, Díaz will not be inch for inch as big as some of the post players in the conference, and even her own locker room, but that slightly smaller size gives the freshman the ability to attack the basket like a Jaloni Cambridge. Díaz can get inside with speed, take on one or two defenders and push defenders back or hit shots from the outside.

"She's got our offense immediately, our defense immediately," Elsa Lemmilä told reporters. "We barely have to coach her because she's doing so well."

Normally, being a freshman in McGuff's system means a lot of learning from the bench. Díaz will have a lot more learning on the court. In previous years, McGuff mentioned how international play separates new college players from those who played high school basketball and AAU alone.

On a Spanish team that features a wealth of Power Four recruits, like UCLA freshman Somto Okafor and Houston point guard Marta Llompart. So, Díaz played alongside college-level talent. UCLA earned two commitments from that Spanish youth team with 6'5 center Anna Smykovskaia set to join the Bruins for the 27-28 season.

All of that to say that Díaz is college basketball ready. It will be no surprise to see Díaz come in to relieve Kylee Kitts or Elsa Lemmilä inside the post, because Díaz can play both roles. Should either of the two bigs miss time due to injury, Díaz can move into the starting lineup.

A 20-minute average per game is not out of the question and that is possibly a low estimate if what Díaz's new teammates say translates onto a college court.

Ohio State's depth does not have a lot of experience. Only Ella Hobbs and Seini Henry are upperclassmen and neither Buckeye started a game yet in their third seasons with the program. There is a strong argument to be made that Díaz is the most experienced player on that bench for McGuff to bring into games, and he will.

Even so, expect a learning curve because Díaz will play some of the best players in the country. Also, teams will begin to figure out her game too. Still, the future looks bright for Díaz in her first season.

articles.title: Athlon Sports has familiar bowl game, opponent projection for Florida
articles.summary: Athlon Sports released its latest bowl game projections after Week 7, with Florida football facing the same team in the same venue as last week.
articles.body:
Last season, Florida football failed to earn a bowl game bid for the second time in three years after appearing in five straight postseason events prior. This fall, the Gators are just one win away from clinching a bowl berth after starting the campaign with four straight wins and a fifth last weekend.

With the dust settled on college football's Week 7 slate, Athlon Sports senior editor released his updated bowl game projections and once again foresees Florida facing Clemson in the Gator Bowl — the same opponent and matchup he predicted last week .

The Gators hold the edge in the all-time series against the Tigers dating back to 1911, with nine wins, three losses and a tie. The last time the two schools faced off on the collegiate gridiron was in 1961 in Gainesville, where the home team prevailed, 21-17; Clemson's last victory came in 1954 — a 14-7 triumph in Jacksonville.

Florida has played in the Gator Bowl nine times dating back to 1952, with seven wins over that span. The last time UF participated in the in-state event came in 2012 during Will Muschamp's first season on the sidelines, beating Ohio State, 24-17. The last time Florida lost a Gator Bowl game was in 1975, when Maryland shut out Doug Dickey's squad, 13-0.

This week, USA TODAY Sports , Sports Illustrated , ESPN and The Athletic also projected Florida to participate in the Gator Bowl against various opponents.

articles.body:
Sure, they play different positions so a direct comparison is not exactly apples to apples, as they say. But New York Rangers defenseman Sean Durzi sure shares quite a few similarities with the guy he was traded for this past summer, Vincent Trocheck .

Just starting physically — they are of similar size (Durzi is 6-foot, 199 pounds; Trocheck 5-foot-11, 187 pounds) with dark hair, and quick smile — dare we say mischievous smirk. Heck, each player has a pretty prominent nose that's clearly taken a knock or two over the years.

Personality-wise, Durzi and Trocheck are both very outgoing, comfortable with the media, funny, honest, and extremely popular with their teammates.

On the ice, even though Durzi is a defenseman and Trocheck a forward, they both bring a strong commitment to playing a diligent two-way game. Each is a right-shot and trusted in all game situations at even strength, as well as on the power play and penalty kill. And neither is to be f***ed with, even if they're far from being the biggest players on the ice.

They even make similar salaries. Durzi takes in $6 million annually and Trocheck makes $5.625 million .

NHL Goals (@nhl_goal_bot) October 19, 2026

Trocheck was a really good Ranger for his four seasons on Broadway from 2022-26. He's missed around here, for sure, and will be even more so if either J.T. Miller or Mika Zibanejad gets injured at any point. The Rangers do not have much center depth, and that's already been proven with trying to fill the 4C role after Joe Veleno sustained a lower-body injury that should sideline him into at least January.

But Durzi, who turned 28 Wednesday and is five years younger than Trocheck, already has helped solidify and improve the Rangers defense corps, partnering with another veteran newcomer — Marcus Pettersson — on the second pair. He's averaging more than 20 minutes a night TOI, has four points (two goals, two assists), and is third on the Rangers with 18 blocked shots in 11 games.

An added bonus is that he's fit perfectly into the locker room and as a respected leader, helping to fill the void created by Trocheck's departure.

The key is for Durzi to remain healthy, something he struggled to do with shoulder issues costing him 74 games the previous two seasons with the Utah Mammoth. He's signed for one more year past this one, but that worry, if that's what we'll call it, is for anoither day.

Right now, Durzi is a real nice fit on Broadway, in all ways, not just one. Just like the player he was traded for used to be.

articles.title: Saints WR Jordyn Tyson will not practice this week
articles.summary: The wait for Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson to make his NFL debut will continue until at least Week 9.
articles.body:
The wait for Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson to make his NFL debut will continue until at least Week 9.

General Manager Mickey Loomis told reporters at a Wednesday press conference that the first-round pick will not practice with the team in Paris ahead of this Sunday's game against the Steelers. Tyson has been out since suffering a hamstring injury in mid-August, although head coach Kellen Moore said that it was unrelated to previous hamstring issues while he was in college.

Loomis said that the rookie is improving and "we feel like we're getting closer," but declined to offer a "specific timetable" for him to get on the field.

The Saints have a bye in Week 8, so their Week 9 home game against the Browns will be the earliest possible date for Tyson to join the lineup. Given the length of his absence and history of hamstring issues, a longer ramp up time might be in the cards once Tyson does return to practice.

articles.title: College Football Big 12 power rankings entering Week 8
articles.summary: Ranking the top teams in the Big 12 entering week 8 in college football.
articles.body:
The rest of this conference needs to thank BYU. Maybe send them flowers. Or a box of Crumbl cookies. By beating Notre Dame in Week 7 of college football , BYU legitimized the entire Big 12. The league has never sent two teams to the CFP and hasn't won a CFP game in the 12-team era.

They were trending towards being CFP afterthoughts again this season after a non-conference slate that just repeatedly saw Big 12 teams lose to Big Ten and SEC foes. But now they have a marquee win they can point to and say this conference can compete with the "blue bloods" of college football.

The Bears will slip a few spots but remain at the bottom of this top-10 list after losing to TCU 14-6. The offense, which had been electric in their 4-game win streak, failed to score a touchdown. DJ Lagway and the rest of the offense still have some work to do.

We have a new entrant in the top-10 this week, thanks to the Mountaineers' 45-42 victory over Cincinnati. Who said Michael Hawkins Jr can't throw? The dual-threat, better known for his running, threw for 464 yards in the win over Cincinnati. This offense is explosive enough to keep them in a lot of ball games.

Three big developments came out of TCU's 14-6 win over Baylor: First, TCU now has a defense. The unit held high-flying Baylor to only 6 points – quite the feat. Second, star RB Jeremy Payne left the game with an injury. They'll need him moving forward. Third, WR Jordan Dwyer played his first full game after an injury in the preseason, and looked awesome. 6 catches for 150 yards. He's going to give a great target for Jaden Craig for the rest of the season.

Is Kansas State good? Probably not. But are they bad? Definitely not. It was a rocky start, but they pulled away from in-state rivals Kansas in a 35-24 victory. Both RB Joe Jackson and QB Avery Johnson rushed for over 130 yards (and that is what Johnson does best).

The Wildcats hold serve at #6 after their Week 7 Bye. They'll have Iowa State coming to town this week before traveling to Lubbock to take on Texas Tech – which could be a potential Noah Fifita legacy game.

They switch places with Houston after their 35-32 defeat at the hands of the Cougars, which felt like an old-school mid-2010s Big 12 matchup. In fact, that's pretty much the whole vibe of this Oklahoma State team – a high-powered offense with a very mediocre defense, just like all of those Big 12 teams from 2014 – 2017.

There goes Conner Weigman putting the team on his back again. For the 3rd game in 4 weeks, the dual-threat QB accounted for every single TD that the Houston offense scored. The showdown at Utah next week is going to determine the trajectory of the second half of the season for the Cougars.

It was a close call, but the Utes escaped Boulder with a 27-24 victory over Colorado in Week 7. The Devon Dampier to Braden Pegan connection continues to dominate, with Pegan scoring twice. Perhaps the poor play was due to looking ahead, as Houston comes to town in Week 8.

In the 53-25 win over Arizona State, the Red Raiders finally looked like we expected them to this season. Will Hammond used his legs to add a new dynamic to the offense, the first-string defense was outstanding, and J'Koby Williams was the dynamic offensive playmaker that we saw him to be last season. This may be the turning point that brings Texas Tech back into National Championship consideration.

Could any other team have been number one? BYU pulled out all the stops to defeat Notre Dame. They ran a fake punt, they ran a double pass, and they had no fear of going for it on 4th down. With no LJ Martin, Bear Bachmeier had to carry both the run and pass game for the offense, and he did it well. The Cougars proved to the nation that they're not just a gimmicky team with a weak schedule – they're true contenders.

articles.title: Kurt Warner shares Fernando Mendoza verdict after what he’s seen from Kirk Cousins

articles.body:
he Las Vegas Raiders have hit a real bump in the road, having lost their last three games, which is raising questions over their quarterback situation.

First time head coach Klint Kubiak made veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins his starter ahead of the 2026 season. Through the opening three games, this looked like a masterstroke from Kubiak as the Raiders went unbeaten.

However, the last three weeks have been a lot more difficult for the Raiders as they have gone 0-3 against the Kansas City Chiefs, New England Patriots and the Buffalo Bills. With the Raiders hitting a spot of turbulence, Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner has shared his verdict on potentially bringing Fernando Mendoza in as the starter.

Kurt Warner urges Raiders not to make Fernando Mendoza their QB1

During the last three games, Cousins has failed to throw for more than two touchdowns in each game. Against the Patriots he was only able to throw for one touchdown. However, the veteran has not been a turnover machine like Sam Darnold with the Seattle Seahawks.

"In my opinion, I don't think they should as of yet. Again, I believe this team is not a great football team, but they've got some key pieces, including Kirk Cousins, that are making them competitive every time out. I just think it's too early right now, with how competitive and how well Kirk is playing, to go to Fernando just yet," Warner said on the Rich Eisen Show.

"It may come a time when you feel like this team is not good enough and not going to make a playoff push, and you make that move. I just don't think the time is right now. I think Kirk gives them confidence right now that, hey, even if we're not winning these games, we're competitive every single time out. I think that is really important for that organisation right now."

Next up for the Raiders is a game against the Los Angeles Rams which could provide them with a big opportunity to get their season back on track. The Rams lost again at the weekend against the Arizona Cardinals as their season continues to derail.

Top spot in the AFC West certainly looks a tough task for the Raiders, but they are still only one win behind the Denver Broncos, who have also looked far from convincing this season. Until the chances of a spot in the postseason is off the cards, Cousins feels like the way forward for Vegas.

articles.title: The Brewers 'Timeless Ticket' issue with the World Series, explained
articles.summary: Some Milwaukee Brewers fans who bought a "Timeless Ticket" ran into an issue with the World Series. Here's why.
articles.body:
A quirky ticketing story has emerged from the awesomeness of the Milwaukee Brewers making it to the 2026 World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays : Back in 2015, the Brewers sold what was called a "Timeless Ticket" for $1,000.

That purchase got fans who bought it quite the perk: A ticket to any game, and that included postseason contests and the World Series. And in the fine print given to Timeless Ticket holders, it said that the Brewers would offer the "best available seat locations subject to ticket availability."

But some fans complained that they were offered standing room tickets, which doesn't seem like the best available seats.

Brewers fans were not happy about the Timeless Ticket issues

Danny Fochesato of Milwaukee bought a Timeless Ticket on his 27th birthday, planning all along to redeem it whenever the Brewers reached the World Series. "Back in 2015, that was a big selling point from the sales people about this," Fochesato said. "They really touted, 'Hey, this is going to be the best available seats. You're getting the priority just behind season ticket holders. Anything the season ticket holders don't have, you'll have dibs at it for the World Series.' That's kind of the story they sold." ... "We had a form, and it only had 400-level or standing-room options," Fochesato said. "We couldn't even know what game we had. We just had to put a preference of which ones we wanted, and then we had to submit the form and just sit and wait for them what we got. I immediately was like, 'No, that's bogus.'"

The Brewers responded to Timeless Ticket fan complaints

Here's what Brewers president of business operations Rick Schlesinger said:

"While we were able to accommodate all with seats, we received feedback from some that they were unhappy with their seat locations. Clearly, even with extraordinary limitations on available seats, we did not live up to the spirit of the program, and we have been working through a resolution."

How the Brewers resolved the Timeless Ticket issues

Per a letter shared on social media by reporters, the decision was made to have those fans keep their World Series tickets that they got, but that they wouldn't count against the Timeless Ticket redemption.

articles.title: How Jalen Ramsey’s edge blitzing unlocked Steelers win over Bucs
articles.summary: Cameron Heyward breaks down how Jalen Ramsey's bookend sacks off the edge sparked the Pittsburgh Steelers' overtime victory.
articles.body:
While defensive coverage headlines typically dominate the chatter around Jalen Ramsey, his deployment as a lethal edge blitzer delivered a masterclass performance in the Pittsburgh Steelers ' overtime victory over Tampa Bay. Ramsey recorded bookend sacks, dropping the quarterback on the opening drive and sealing the game in overtime, proving to be the catalyst for Pittsburgh's front seven.

During an appearance on " Not Just Football with Cam Heyward ," defensive veteran Cameron Heyward provided a high-level technical breakdown of Ramsey's rare instinct and precision off the edge.

"Well, I don't know how many guys have done this, but in a game to get a sack on the first drive and the last drive is pretty special," Heyward noted. "And Jalen times his blitzes up better than anybody. He explodes into the backfield. He's able to just time it up perfectly."

Rather than lining up directly on the line of scrimmage, Ramsey frequently disguises his rush from depth. This allows the front seven to manipulate blocking schemes and the offensive line's eyes. On the game-winning play in overtime, Pittsburgh showed a heavy front that forced Tampa Bay's protection to slide away from Ramsey, granting him a clear runway to close out the game.

"On the last play in particular, we had a lot of guys at the line and it requires a lot of detail," Heyward explained. "Not only Jalen, but T.J. [Watt], myself, Nick [Herbig], Pat [Queen], to take the eyes of the offensive lineman, and then it allows Jalen to just get a free shot, and Jalen made him pay. The execution on that last play was flawless."

By pairing pre-snap manipulation with Ramsey's elite closing speed, Pittsburgh has unlocked a game-altering pressure package. Ramsey's ability to time up his rushes and deliver high-impact plays in critical moments gives the Steelers a dynamic pass-rushing threat off the edge.

articles.title: Packers vs. Lions Week 7 TV Broadcast Map
articles.summary: Good news, (almost) everyone!
articles.body:
When the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions meet up for their first of two 2026 regular season matchups on Sunday afternoon, nearly every media market in the United States will get to see the game on local television. These two teams have combined for five playoff appearances in the past three years, and both come into Week 7 with a winning record; as a result, FOX made it their late-afternoon game of the week when the NFL announced its schedule in May, and that slot has held up despite some early-season struggles on the Packers' part.

In fact, the Packers have bounced back remarkably from a 1-2 start that saw their game against the Chicago Bears two weeks ago — also initially slated for a large viewership in the 3:25 PM window — get flexed back into the early afternoon. (To be fair, the injury to Bears quarterback Caleb Williams surely factored in as well.) Green Bay now sits at 4-2 and on a three-game winning streak, while the Lions are 3-2 and coming off a bye week.

These two teams have combined for some great games in the past few years, though 2025 saw the Packers sweep Detroit for the first time in Dan Campbell's tenure as head coach of the Lions. Detroit is currently favored by 3 points, but this game very much feels like a tossup, especially if the Lions' last-ranked passing defense continues to play the way it has to this point in the season.

Ready to watch some fireworks? Good, because unless you're in California and Nevada, you're getting this game on your local FOX affiliate. The only other game on FOX in this time slot is Rams-Raiders, which will have a very limited local viewing area this week. As the top game on the network this week, Packers and Lions fans will get the network's top broadcast tandem of Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady. Burkhardt has a day off from his duties as the pregame and postgame panel host for the World Series, but he's not traveling far — games 1 and 2 will be held in Milwaukee on Friday and Saturday nights, giving him a short flight over Lake Michigan for Sunday's game at Ford Field before he presumably makes a trip down to Tampa for Monday's game 3.
